prompt: Model a fixed-size connection pool with checkout and return, including the guard that stops a connection being handed out twice. Complete PooledConnectionManager.
explanation: A pool exists because opening a database connection is slow, so a fixed set is created once and then lent out and returned. Two lists -- idle and busy -- make the invariant obvious: a connection is in exactly one of them, never both and never neither. The guard in release is the part that matters: checking that the connection really was checked out (List.remove returns true only when it was there) is what stops a careless double-release from putting the same connection in the idle list twice and handing it to two callers at once.
hints: The constructor is a simple loop: for (int i = 1; i <= size; i++) idle.add(new FakeDbConnection(i)).
For checkout, scan the idle list for the smallest id, then remove it from idle and add it to busy before returning it.
busy.remove(connection) returns a boolean -- use that as the test for whether the connection was really checked out, and only add it back to idle when it returns true.
